No recording without written permission. Honest work: your own, with sources cited in APA style. Fictional or open data only: never personal information about real people.
Recorded representations of facts — numbers, text, dates — in a formalised form that can be stored, transmitted and processed. By themselves they contain no conclusion.
Data that have been processed and placed in a context, so that they have a meaning for the person who receives them. A decision is taken on the basis of information.
An organised collection of logically related data, stored together with its metadata (the description of the data: names, types, units, rules).
The software that creates the database, keeps it up to date and controls every access to it. No user and no program reads or writes the stored data directly.

Front: What is data integrity, and how does a DBMS protect it?
Back: The accuracy and consistency of the stored data. The designer declares constraints; the DBMS checks them at every insertion and change and refuses a row that breaks one.

Front: What is the difference between a flat file and a file-based database?
Back: A flat file is one table in one file, with no rules and no declared types (for example a CSV file). A file-based database is a complete DBMS that runs inside the program and keeps the database in one file, with no server: SQLite, DuckDB.

All data are in tables of rows and columns; a primary key identifies each row; foreign keys link the tables; the language is SQL; constraints and transactions keep related data correct under many users.

Front: Name the four kinds of non-relational database and the typical question of each.
Back: Document: the whole record at once. Key-value: the value for this key. Wide-column: very many writes of rows found by a key. Graph: paths through relationships.

Front: What makes data 'big', and which two techniques answer it?
Back: Volume, speed of arrival or variety beyond what one machine can store and process in an acceptable time. Columnar storage (Apache Parquet) and distributed processing (Apache Spark).

Front: Why is the alteration of an old entry in a blockchain detected?
Back: Each block stores the hash of the previous block. Changing an entry changes the hash of its block, so the value stored in the next block no longer matches: tamper evidence.
Data that describe other data: the name of a column, its type, its unit, its rule. Without metadata the value 9.80 cannot be interpreted.
The same fact stored in more than one place, for example a customer's city in the orders file and in the customers file.
Copies of the same fact that no longer agree: 'Madrid' in one row and 'MADRID' in another.
The structure of the data is described once, in the database, so a change of structure is not repeated in every program.
A rule declared by the designer — not empty, unique, greater than zero — that the DBMS checks at every insertion and change.
The DBMS orders the operations of simultaneous users so that no change is lost and nobody reads a half-finished change.
A program that carries out a task for its users — taking an order, drawing a chart — by sending requests to the DBMS.
The primary key identifies each row of a table uniquely. A foreign key must match a primary key in another table: this is how tables are linked.
Software whose licence allows anyone to use it for any purpose, to read and modify its source code, and to redistribute it. The OSI keeps the list of approved licences.
